summary: Errors are normal and useful. An error message usually tells you exactly what SQLite couldn't understand.
points: "near ...: syntax error" means a word or symbol is misplaced or misspelled. Look just before the word it names.
"no such table" and "no such column" mean a name is misspelled or doesn't exist.
Text values need single quotes. Without them, SQLite reads the word as a column name.
Some mistakes give no error, only a wrong result, so always check the output. Build queries one small step at a time.

example.explanation: This runs without an error but is wrong. With no comma, price becomes a new name for title, so only one column appears.
